title: The Branches of Philosophy
objective: After this level you can name the main branches of philosophy (metaphysics, epistemology, ethics, logic, aesthetics and political philosophy) and the question each one asks.
summary: Metaphysics asks what exists, epistemology what we can know, ethics what is right, logic what is good reasoning, aesthetics what is beautiful, and political philosophy what makes a society just.

cards.headline: Every philosophical question has a home address.
cards.body: Does anything truly exist? Is it wrong to lie? Is this painting beautiful? Different questions live in different branches. Here’s the map.

items.label: Metaphysics
points: What is the world made of?

items.label: Ethics
points: What makes an action right or wrong?

cards.headline: A name that was an accident
cards.body: Metaphysics sounds mystical, but the name is a filing label. At least a century after Aristotle died, an editor, probably Andronicus of Rhodes, grouped some of his books as Ta meta ta phusika: “the ones after the physical ones”, meaning after his Physics. Aristotle never knew the word. The deepest-sounding branch of philosophy is named after a spot on a shelf.

cards.headline: Three more branches
cards.body: Logic studies good and bad arguments and reasoning: the very tool Level 1 said philosophy runs on. Aesthetics is the theory of beauty and, more broadly, the philosophy of art. Political philosophy begins with one question: what should a person’s relationship to society be? From there it asks what makes a society just or unjust.

cards.headline: One night, three branches
cards.body: Try the map on a single puzzle. You dream you’re flying. Does the dream world exist in any sense? That’s metaphysics. Can you be sure you’re awake right now? Epistemology. Is it fine to tell friends you really flew, to sound interesting? Ethics. One strange night, three branches, each asking its own kind of question.

cards.headline: The Branches of Philosophy: the big picture
learned: Ethics: right, wrong and the good life
